record.original_question: Archimedean copulas are copulas generated by additive generators. For dimension 2, every associative 2-copula C: [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] with C(x, x) < x for all x in (0, 1) is Archimedean. Is there an algebraic characterization of Archimedean 3-copulas, and more generally of Archimedean n-copulas for n > 2?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.2. Copulas generated by means of additive generators are called Archimedean copulas.
Each associative 2-copula C : [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] is Archimedean whenever C(x, x) < x for all x in ]0, 1[.
Is there an algebraic characterization for Archimedean 3-copulas (or, generally, for n-copulas with n > 2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An n-copula is a function C: [0,1]^n → [0,1] that is the joint cumulative distribution function of a random vector (U_1, ..., U_n) each of whose marginals is uniform on [0,1]; equivalently, C is grounded, has uniform univariate marginals, and is n-increasing. An n-copula C is called Archimedean if there exists a continuous, strictly decreasing function φ: [0,1] → [0,∞] with φ(1) = 0 (called an additive generator) such that
   C(u_1, ..., u_n) = φ^{[-1]}(φ(u_1) + ··· + φ(u_n))   for all (u_1,...,u_n) ∈ [0,1]^n,
where φ^{[-1]} denotes the pseudo-inverse of φ. A 2-copula C is associative if C(C(x,y),z) = C(x, C(y,z)) for all x,y,z ∈ [0,1]; it is known that every associative 2-copula C satisfying C(x,x) < x for all x ∈ (0,1) is Archimedean.

Problem. Provide an algebraic characterization of Archimedean 3-copulas, and more generally of Archimedean n-copulas for n > 2; that is, find a set of purely algebraic (functional-equation type) conditions on an n-copula C that are equivalent to C being Archimedean.
artifact.status_search_result: Several algebraic-style characterizations of n-dimensional Archimedean copulas have been proposed (e.g., the Jouini–Clemen characterization, and characterizations via n-ary associativity in the sense of Post, alongside differential and diagonal characterizations). Associative n-copulas in the Post sense have been shown to be n-ary extensions of associative 2-copulas with special constraints, and associative copulas decompose as ordinal sums of Archimedean copulas and the minimum copula. A definitive, universally accepted purely algebraic characterization analogous to the 2-dimensional case still does not appear to be settled, so the problem can be considered partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Associative n-dimensional copulas
status_evidence.snippet: Associativity of n-dimensional copulas in the sense of Post is studied; such copulas are n-ary extensions of associative 2-dimensional copulas with special constraints.
status_evidence.claim: Post-associativity provides a partial algebraic framework for n-copulas relating to Archimedean ones.

status_evidence.title: Multivariate Archimedean copulas, d-monotone functions
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes Archimedean n-copulas via d-monotone generators.
status_evidence.claim: Analytic (d-monotone) rather than purely algebraic characterization exists.

status_evidence.title: Dependence Modeling with Archimedean Copulas (Nelsen)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Archimedean copulas including multivariate extensions.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references discuss generator-based but not purely algebraic n-dimensional characterizations.
